newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LATE RALLY GIVES DODGERS VICTORY OVER CARDINALS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LATE RALLY GIVES DODGERS VICTORY OVER CARDINALS.

text.p: Tim Wallach capped a four-run, eighth-inning rally with a two-run single as the Los Angeles Dodgers maintained a half-game lead in the National League West with a 6-5 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals.
With two outs in the eighth and men on first and second, the Cardinals brought in ace reliever Dennis Eckersley to face Raul Mondesi and protect a 5-2 lead.
Mondesi singled in one run and Eric Karros followed with a ground-rule double to make it a one-run game. Wallach then singled between third and shortstop to put the Dodgers on top.

"They had a lot of opportunities and they didn't cash in until I got out there," said Eckersley, who started Mondesi, Karros and Wallach with 0-2 counts. "Mondesi's at-bat was the at-bat, I just couldn't put him away."
Scott Radinsky (4-1) pitched two scoreless innings for the win and Todd Worrell tossed a perfect ninth for his 43rd save.
The Dodgers took three of four from the Central-Division leaders and have won six of their last seven overall to remain ahead of second-place San Diego in the West.
"This was a big-league heartbreaker," said Cards manager Tony La Russa. The Cardinals have lost four of five but maintained their 2 1/2 game lead over Houston.
In San Diego, Joey Hamilton and Willie Blair combined on an eight-hitter as San Diego blanked the Cincinnati Reds 8-0.
Hamilton (14-8) gave up all eight hits and one walk with two strikeouts over six innings. Blair worked three perfect innings for the save.

San Diego, who have won six of seven overall and 11 of 13 at home, remained one-half game behind Los Angeles for first place in the National League West. The Padres extended their advantage to 1 1/2 games over Montreal for the wild-card spot.

In New York, Tom Glavine allowed two runs over 8 2/3 innings and Chipper Jones had a pair of RBI singles as the Atlanta Braves ended their season-high six-game losing streak with a 3-2 win over the New York Mets.
The Braves, who snapped a 10-game road losing streak, reduced their magic number to nine for clinching a fifth straight division title. They lead Montreal by 5 1/2 games in the National League East.
Glavine (14-9) walked one and struck out nine. The Mets put runners on the corners with two out in the ninth but Mark Wohlers came on to strike out Andy Tomberlin to end the game.

In Montreal, Al Leiter combined with two relievers on a six-hitter and Jeff Conine homered and drove in two runs as the Florida Marlins held on for a 4-3 victory over the Montreal Expos to avoid a four-game sweep.
Leiter (15-12) allowed three runs and five hits over 6 1/3 innings with three walks and nine strikeouts.
At Colorado, Andres Galarraga homered twice and had four RBI as the Colorado Rockies won their eighth straight, 11-4 over the Houston Astros.
Colorado's surge has moved them within 4 1/2 games of the National League wild-card berth with 12 games remaining.

Galarraga hit his 44th homer in the second off starter Doug Drabek (6-9) to pull the Rockies within 2-1. His second homer, a three-run shot, extended the lead to 11-2. Colorado's Ellis Burks became the first Rockie with 200 hits in a season.
Houston has lost three straight and 11 of 15 to fall three games behind first-place St. Louis in the NL Central.
In San Francisco, the Pittsburgh Pirates scored six times in the 10th inning then withstood a four-run Giants rally in their half to take an 11-9 victory and complete a doubleheader sweep.
Jon Lieber threw seven strong innings and John Wehner drove in a pair of runs as the Pirates beat the Giants 4-1 in the opener. Lieber (8-5) allowed one run and nine hits with six strikeouts.

In the nightcap, Giants star Barry Bonds stole his 30th base, joining the 30-30 (at least 30 homers and 30 steals in a season) club for the fourth time. Only his father, Bobby, who achieved the feat five times, has done it more.
The sweep ran Pittsburgh's winning streak to five games.
In Chicago, Benito Santiago homered three times and drove in all six runs and Curt Schilling tossed his league-leading seventh complete game as the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Chicago Cubs 6-1.
Santiago led off the second against Kevin Foster (7-4) with his 27th homer. The Phillies increased the lead to 4-0 in the sixth when Santiago belted a three-run homer.
He capped the scoring in the eighth by stroking a two-run homer off reliever Kent Bottenfield.
